tools.description: Explain whether one exact package version can be installed from a repository and, if not, why. Use it when an install fails with 404 or 403 for a version that should exist, or before pinning a version. Returns available (true/false) and reasons, each with a source: min_age (the version is younger than the repository's minimum age; until is when it unlocks), curation (a curation rule or the allowlist hides it; rule_id names the rule, detail quotes its reason), quarantine (a vulnerability or secret scan quarantined it), license_policy, repository_blocked, or not_found (a hosted repository stores no such package version, judged on the names get_package lists). Also returns published_at and min_age: off (no minimum age), checked, or unknown (the publish time is not cached yet, so the age cannot be judged). A proxy repository is judged on its cached upstream metadata; the upstream is never asked. A group repository has no verdict of its own: use check_dependencies, which answers for a group (also for one version), or ask its members, which get_repository lists in group order with the rule that decides between them. Requires read permission on the repository.

tools.description: Check many package versions at once (a lockfile, or the dependencies you are about to add) against a repository, including a group. Returns one result per package version, in order, each with status: available, held (reasons as in check_availability), not_found (no member has the version) or unknown (a proxy has not cached the package's metadata, so whether it has the version cannot be told; install or fetch the package once), and repository, the member that decided. A group decides like serving does: the first member that has the version decides even when it holds it back, and unless merge_proxy_versions is set a package a hosted member holds is decided by the hosted members only.
